annotations.title: Choose which senders' emails are tracked, for which topics

description: The senders whose emails the person tracks, each for one or more topics (a track's schemaId; every track on a topic gets them). This is the usual way to track email: add the sender for the track's topic, have them forward one of its emails (or send_message one you can read), and TrackerHacker makes the hack from it by itself, from a community hack for the sender or drafted with AI, and tells the person when its row is in. When it isn't sure (or AI fixes are off in their Settings), the email waits in the Inbox: then write the hack yourself (save_hack). action list shows the routes and the topics the person has tracks on; add takes sender (an address or domain), optional subjects (words the subject must have, for one sender who sends several kinds) and topics, or trackId for that track's topic, and merges with the same sender and subjects; set_topics takes id and topics (at least one). Removing a sender is the person's, under Emails you track in the app. While automatic forwarding from Gmail is on, a new sender's last 30 days of mail are read in now.

id.description: set_topics: the route's id, from list.

subjects.description: add: words the subject must have; leave out for all of the sender's emails.

topics.description: Topic ids (a track's schemaId from list_tracks).

trackId.description: add: instead of topics, this track's topic.
